title: Three SST products with matched means raise calculated tropical cyclone potential intensity by 3.4-4.1 m/s in 2023-2024 at fixed NCEP R2 profiles
abstract: We tested how recent NCEP R2 sea temperature shifts enter tropical cyclone potential intensity (PI). We held monthly atmospheric profiles fixed and substituted ERSSTv5, OISSTv2.1 or COBE-SST2. Each source was matched to the R2 2010-2019 mean at each grid point and calendar month. The common test has 493 ocean points at absolute latitudes 5-25 degrees and 516 months in 1982-2024. Substitution raises the 2023-2024 minus 2010-2019 tropical PI change by 3.4-4.1 m/s. The Atlantic season effect is 5.5-6.5 m/s. Native R2 PI falls by 3.28 m/s between these epochs; all three matched sources remove this fall at the same atmospheric state. A fixed warm-water mask retains a tropical effect of 3.65-4.25 m/s and removes the cold-profile negative responses found in a +0.1 K numerical test. The 2001-2024 PI trend remains source-dependent after substitution, so its sign is unresolved. This is a fixed-profile diagnostic effect, not an estimate of storm wind change or the full response of a corrected reanalysis. Atmospheric errors, shared source data, monthly means, coarse sampling and only two target years limit inference. Code, aggregate results, figures, source hashes and retrieval instructions are included.

display.caption: Native R2 minus mean-matched source SST and calculated potential intensity. The atmosphere is fixed. The basin bars give the difference in the 2023-2024 minus 2010-2019 change.
Native and ERSSTv5-substituted seasonal potential intensity anomalies use the same atmospheric profiles. They are environmental limits, not storm winds.
